prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: production transparent animated VFX sprite atlas for a fixed overhead Korean historical fantasy tower-defense game.
Input image 1 is a material and painted rendering reference only; create NEW frames, do not copy its eight-cell layout.
Primary request: A clockwise teal-blue wave ring gradually rises, with exactly three small cool silver meteor fragments entering the water and making white foam. Water and falling stars fuse, then settle into scattered silver-blue ripples. No fire.
Layout is mandatory: exactly 16 separate animation frames in a precise FOUR COLUMNS by FOUR ROWS square grid. Read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. All sixteen cells equally sized, with the same stable central ground origin and identical fixed overhead/isometric viewpoint (about 60 degrees looking down). Draw the ground effect as a nearly circular ring seen slightly from above; the game will lay this texture on the ground. At least 12 percent transparent padding inside every cell, including around stray motes. Nothing touches or overlaps any neighboring cell. Each cell has ONE complete effect, not multiple effects.
Animation: cells 1-3 gentle small gathering; 4-6 growing; 7-9 clear peak; 10-12 dispersing; 13-16 smaller wisps and quiet fade. The scale can grow within the cell but center must remain fixed. Sixteen successive unique frames with small coherent changes, not random designs.
Style: premium hand-painted stylized 3D game illustration, sculpted rounded volumes, finely painted reflective highlights and soft edged smoke, harmonious restrained tones matching reference, readable at a small battlefield scale. No neon outlines, no flat vector shapes, no crude geometric symbols.
Background: true fully transparent alpha, no floor, no shadows, no black or colored backdrop, no checkerboard, no labels, no borders, no numbers, no letters, no watermark. Canvas square.
rejection: Baked isometric perspective was unsuitable for a ground-plane texture
